# Grocery lists for the sample menus

One checklist per sample menu, for one person for a week, generated from the menus so the amounts always match. Tick items off on your phone or print the page. Fresh food over packaged: more than 70 % of the sodium people eat comes from packaged and restaurant food, and phosphate additives are absorbed almost completely.

## Staples for every menu

- [ ] Herbs and spices without salt (black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, oregano, cumin, cinnamon)
- [ ] A salt-free seasoning blend whose label does **not** list potassium chloride
- [ ] Lemons or bottled lemon juice, cider or balsamic vinegar, fresh garlic
- [ ] Olive or canola oil, unsalted butter, mayonnaise
- [ ] Low-sodium ketchup and yellow mustard
- [ ] Glucose tablets or gel for lows: keep them at home, in the car and in your bag

!!! tip "Check the label for"

    - **"PHOS" in the ingredient list** (phosphoric acid, sodium phosphate, any "…phosphate"): choose another brand. Phosphorus is not required on the US Nutrition Facts label.
    - **Potassium chloride or other potassium salts**, often in salt substitutes and "reduced sodium" soups, sauces and deli meats.
    - **Sodium per serving:** 140 mg or less is "low sodium"; 460 mg or more (20 % DV) is high.
    - **Fresh meat or poultry "enhanced", "self-basting" or "injected" with a solution:** it adds sodium and phosphate. Buy plain.
    - **Total carbohydrate × the servings you will eat**, for your insulin plan.
